Natijada, Qo‘shma Shtatlar Osiyo va Tinch okeani hududi osmonini deyarli to‘liq nazorat qila oladigan bo‘ladi. Panetta ochiq e’lon qildi: AQSh siyosatining bosh maqsadi – hududda ustunlikni kuchaytirish va ayniqsa Xitoy tahdidiga qarshi mustahkam javob berish. Mazkur kelishuv Amerika uchun Avstraliya dengiz portlariga ustuvor kirish va ulardan foydalanish kafolatini beradi. Avvalgi yillardan farqli ravishda, bu yil sammitda Xitoy eng muhim muhokama mavzusi bo‘ldi, biroq AQSh va Avstraliya rasmiylari bu haqda ommaga ochiq gapirishmadi.
translated_content: US Secretary of Defense Leon Panetta and Australian officials recently signed a major agreement: alongside a radar system and space telescope, secret satellite monitoring will also be set up in Australia. This means the United States will have near-total control of the sky over the Asia-Pacific region. Panetta made it clear: the main goal of US policy is to strengthen dominance in the region, especially with a firm response to the threat from China. Several analysts believe this agreement is aimed squarely at China, and at the US-Australia security summit, the deal clearly shifts the balance of power in the region in favor of the US. More than 3,000 US troops are being deployed in Australia, with a main mission to defend key strategic locations. Australian Defense Minister Steven Smith says US air and naval personnel have been stationed at the main military bases. This agreement guarantees the US priority access and use of Australian seaports. Unlike previous years, this year’s summit saw China as the main subject of discussion, though US and Australian officials avoided addressing this openly in public.

article_content: 去年11月，理大警民衝突激烈爆發。網民即時號召「營救」被困示威者，當時年僅24歲的地盤工黎振鴻，被指清晨攜帶炸藥與多枚汽油彈，衝向載警車襲擊警方。他早前承認企圖縱火等兩罪，被還押至今日宣判。法官胡雅文強調，案件顯示高度組織性及嚴密計劃，甚至聯繫多位同夥攜帶武器一同參與暴力事件。她指出他不僅向警車投擲汽油彈，還意圖引爆炸藥，明顯以警察為目標，行為嚴重威脅社會安全。經衡量多項因素，最終判處黎振鴻入獄5年。 被告黎振鴻（24歲，地盤工）被控有意圖而企圖縱火、於公眾地方持有攻擊性武器兩罪。案發於去年11月18日，旺角黑布街與豉油街交界，他涉嫌用火與炸藥摧毀警車，意圖損壞車輛並危害司機及路人安全。當天他還在黑布街公眾地方持有多把刀、多支伸縮棍和胡椒噴霧。另外，黎振鴻還因涉嫌管有爆炸品意圖損壞財產而被起訴，該案存檔法院。
translated_content: Last November, violent clashes between police and protesters broke out at PolyU. Netizens quickly called for a 'rescue' of trapped protesters. At that time, 24-year-old construction worker Lai Chun-hung was accused of carrying explosives and multiple petrol bombs at dawn, charging at a police van and attacking officers. He had earlier pleaded guilty to attempted arson and related charges and was remanded until sentencing today. Judge Wu Yaman stressed that the case demonstrated a high level of organization and detailed planning, including coordinating with several accomplices to participate in violent acts. She noted that he not only threw petrol bombs at the police van, but also intended to detonate explosives, clearly targeting the police and seriously threatening public safety. After considering multiple factors, Lai Chun-hung was ultimately sentenced to five years in prison. Defendant Lai Chun-hung (24, construction worker) was charged with attempted arson with intent and possession of offensive weapons in a public place. The incident took place on November 18 last year at the intersection of Nathan Road and Soy Street in Mong Kok. He was alleged to have used fire and explosives to destroy a police vehicle, intending to damage the vehicle and endanger the driver and passersby. On the same day, he also possessed multiple knives, batons, and pepper spray in public. Additionally, Lai Chun-hung was charged with possession of explosives with intent to damage property, which was filed at court.

article_content: 2019年3月31日，土耳其地方选举爆发了全国性震撼，对总统埃尔多安来说简直是一场前所未有的灾难。消息称，执政党AKP很有可能痛失安卡拉和伊斯坦布尔两大市长职位。初步统计中，反对派大幅领先，甚至有专家警示这或成为政权更替的新起点。更离奇的是，双方都宣布获胜，局势极度混乱。 伊斯坦布尔记者亚历山大·比耶特报道： “目前伊斯坦布尔没有正式结果，两位候选人仅相差4000票，而总投票人数高达900万。AKP则严厉质疑投票过程，指称选举或遭人为操控，要求彻底重新计票，两市局势一触即发。 对埃尔多安总统来说，这不仅仅是一次沉重的个人打击，更可能直接威胁到整个国家的稳定。他像打总统选战一样投入地方选举，结果却遭遇惨败，声誉尽毁。局势极有可能引爆全国性大规模抗议浪潮，政权根基岌岌可危。 观察人士指出，这次选举结果，一方面因为选民对连续多次投票极度疲惫，另一方面则是因经济危机恶化，社会怒气已经无法控制。现在还有传闻说，境外势力正趁机挑动骚乱，意在颠覆现政权。土耳其人民的愤怒已到达危险极限。” 最终，这成为选民对埃尔多安的严重警告。竞选期间他刻意回避谈及经济困境，而这恰恰是全民最关心的主题。有分析称，如果当局继续逃避现实，土耳其极可能滑向全面混乱。
translated_content: On March 31, 2019, Turkey’s local elections sent shockwaves across the country—an unprecedented disaster for President Erdogan. Reports say the ruling AKP is almost certain to lose the mayor’s seats in both Ankara and Istanbul. Early data shows the opposition massively ahead, with some experts warning this may signal the start of regime change. Bizarrely, both sides claim victory, causing utter chaos. Reporter Alexandre Billette from Istanbul: "So far there is no official result in Istanbul. The two candidates are separated by just 4,000 votes, out of 9 million cast. The AKP has raised serious doubts about the voting process, alleging possible manipulation and demanding a complete recount—tensions are running high in both cities. For President Erdogan, this is not just a personal blow, but could directly threaten the stability of the nation. He campaigned for local elections as if they were a presidential race, yet ended up defeated, his reputation ruined. The situation could well spark mass protests nationwide, putting the regime’s foundations at risk. Observers note the results are partly due to voter fatigue from recurrent ballots, but even more because of a worsening economic crisis fueling intense public anger. Now, rumors are swirling that foreign forces are stirring unrest, aiming to bring down the current regime. The anger among Turkish people is reaching a dangerous threshold." Ultimately, this stands as a serious warning to Erdogan from voters. During the campaign he dodged talk of the economic crisis—the very issue that’s on everyone’s minds. Some say, if the government keeps hiding from reality, Turkey could plunge into total chaos.

最近，圍繞烏茲別克記者哈伊魯洛·哈米多夫被監禁的討論，使該國言論自由的困境再次成為熱議話題。歐洲安全與合作組織（OSCE）媒體自由代表杜尼婭·米亞托維奇公開呼籲釋放哈米多夫及另外兩名被拘押記者。BBC烏茲別克語新聞部也在社交媒體上發起討論，邀請公眾發表對哈米多夫案及國內言論自由現狀的看法。

然而，真正參加討論並願意表達觀點的用戶非常少。有網友博季拉利認為，言論自由應該存在，但哈米多夫曾直言描述哈里發國等敏感問題，這十分複雜。另一位Facebook用戶伊布拉希姆·波爾沃諾夫則悲觀指出：“烏茲別克根本沒有真正的法律，憲法只是個童話。你一開口說實話，自己的下場可想而知。”

針對這一敏感議題受到冷淡回應、留言極少的現象，BBC烏茲別克語新聞部專訪了曾任烏茲別克國家廣播公司記者的納爾祖拉·奧洪茹諾夫，就輿論不活躍的原因以及言論自由現況進行了深入討論。
translated_content:
Recently, the imprisonment of Uzbek journalist Xayrullo Hamidov has brought renewed attention to the issue of free speech in the country. Dunya Mijatovic, OSCE’s media freedom representative, publicly called for the release of Hamidov and two other detained journalists. The BBC Uzbek Service started a discussion on social media, encouraging people to share their thoughts about Hamidov’s case and the overall state of free speech in Uzbekistan.

Despite this, only a handful of people chose to join the conversation or voice their opinions. One user, Botirali, remarked that while freedom of speech is important, Hamidov’s outspoken comments on sensitive issues like the caliphate make things very complicated. Another Facebook user, Ibrohim Polvonov, expressed his frustration, stating, “There is no real law in Uzbekistan; the constitution is just a fairy tale. If you speak out, you know what will happen to you.”

To understand why this topic received so little public engagement and so few comments, the BBC Uzbek Service interviewed Narzulla Oxunjonov, a former journalist at the national broadcast company, to discuss the reasons behind the silence and the realities of free speech.
